raw_response:
I'm 73 this year, farming these same 12 mu in Quzhou for 55 years. With just my wife and me in the household now, every mu has to pay its way, and every jin of fertilizer has to be justified. I have education—agricultural training years ago—so I understand the technical side, but at this age, my body writes checks that my knowledge can't always cash.

I keep 10 mu in wheat-maize double cropping. That's our bread and butter. The wheat goes in right after maize harvest, around October 10th. I plant Jimai 22, an improved variety I've used for years. For fertilizer, I target 17 kg N per mu—less than the extension recommendation of 20, but at my age I won't borrow money for inputs. I split it: 10 kg N as compound at planting, 7 kg urea at jointing in March. Three irrigations—winter, jointing, and filling. The well never fails but pumping costs about 20 yuan per mu each time, so I don't waste water.

Maize follows wheat in mid-June. Zhengdan 958 hybrid, 15 kg N per mu all at planting, two irrigations. The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is maybe 5 days. No time for deep tillage—rotary till and plant immediately.

Cotton is down to 2 mu now. Used to be more, but picking is young people's work. I hire help but it's 100 yuan a day. I keep those 2 mu because cotton cash income is reliable and the soil there is lighter, better suited for it. Plant in late April, 12 kg N per mu, irrigate twice.

Total input costs will be about 7,300 yuan. That's most of our cash reserve, but without spending on inputs, yields drop and then we're worse off. My biggest risk is labor—if the hired hands don't show up at harvest, my wife and I can't carry the load alone.
